open_questions: [agentic-loops] Codex has no documented per-run turn/budget-cap flag analogous to Claude's maxTurns/maxBudgetUsd - it relies on sandbox/approval limits, account usage limits, reasoning_effort, and human review. Is there a supported way to hard-cap a single codex exec run's token/dollar spend from the CLI, or must that be enforced externally (CI timeout / spend circuit breaker)?

[agentic-loops] Exact Claude Code OTEL metric names (e.g. claude_code.token.usage vs claude_code.cost.usage) and their full attribute sets live in the /monitoring-usage reference, which I did not fetch line-by-line; names should be pinned against that reference before hard-coding dashboards, and trace span names are explicitly beta.

[agentic-loops] Claude Routines and Codex Automations are both explicitly in research preview / recently shipped (Routines ~2026-04-14, /fire API behind the experimental-cc-routine-2026-04-01 beta header). API shapes, rate limits, and daily-run caps may change; the specific per-account/hourly GitHub-webhook caps are shown in-product rather than documented as fixed numbers.

[agentic-loops] The 'unrolling the Codex agent loop' framing (each turn ends with an assistant message signaling a termination state) came from search summaries because the OpenAI post returned 403 to direct fetch; the mechanic is corroborated by Codex loop docs but the primary source wasn't read in full.

[agentic-loops] No official, quantified guidance was found on optimal self-paced /loop intervals or on when a fresh-model condition evaluator (/goal) meaningfully outperforms the working model deciding it's done - this remains heuristic and workflow-dependent.

[agentic-loops] Cross-platform cost figures (runaway-bill anecdotes, 55-75% savings) come from news/vendor sources, not audited benchmarks, so they justify the direction of the practice but shouldn't be cited as precise expectations.

[hooks] Exact delivery mechanism and full field schema of Codex CLI's `notify` program payload (argv positional argument vs stdin; whether the `type` value is 'agent-turn-complete' and what other fields like turn-id / input-messages / last-assistant-message are included) — the official advanced-config page was unreachable at fetch time, so this should be verified against the installed Codex version.

[hooks] Whether/when Codex CLI will actually execute `type:"prompt"` and `type:"agent"` hook handlers (currently parsed but skipped), which would enable judgment-based gates portable from Claude Code.

[hooks] Precise per-version availability of Claude Code's newer/rarer events (Setup, TeammateIdle, TaskCreated/TaskCompleted, WorktreeCreate/Remove, Elicitation/ElicitationResult) — the docs enumerate ~32 events but real availability depends on the installed CLI build and some are clearly recent additions.
[hooks] Concrete production benchmarks on the token/latency cost of prompt- and agent-based Stop gates versus deterministic command gates, to guide when the added LLM verification is worth it.

[hooks] Cross-platform robustness details for Windows hook execution (Git Bash vs command_windows/commandWindows overrides) under real CI, where trust prompts and shell differences most often break hooks.

[session-management] The exact context-utilization threshold that triggers automatic compaction in Claude Code is not officially published and varies by model and window size (e.g., 200K vs 1M / Sonnet 5); practitioner figures (~70-80%) are unverified against Anthropic docs.

[session-management] Whether the Codex model_context_window auto-compaction regression (issue #16068) is fixed in the current release, and which exact versions are affected, is unconfirmed from official changelog sources.

[session-management] No official published cadence exists for proactive /compact vs /clear (e.g., 'every 30-45 min'); such numbers come from third-party blogs, not Anthropic/OpenAI, and are workload-dependent.

[session-management] How teams using BOTH Claude Code (auto memory in ~/.claude/projects/.../memory/) and API agents (client-side /memories memory tool) should reconcile or share a single source of truth is not documented; auto memory is machine-local with no official cross-machine sync.

[session-management] Codex's compaction quality/fidelity and its equivalent of Claude's 'what survives compaction' guarantees (e.g., whether AGENTS.md is re-injected post-compaction) are not clearly documented; Codex's exact compaction internals are less transparent than Claude Code's.
[session-management] The widely cited '7-hour autonomous run' figure for Codex is associated with model marketing and practitioner write-ups rather than a precise, reproducible spec in official docs.

[repo-setup] Claude Code still does not natively read AGENTS.md as of mid-2026 (requires an @AGENTS.md import or symlink); the team has signaled openness to standardizing once features stabilize, so native support could land and change the recommended unification pattern — re-verify against code.claude.com/docs/en/memory.

[repo-setup] Exact model identifiers move fast (Codex docs reference gpt-5.4/gpt-5.5; Claude Code references Opus/Sonnet/Haiku tiers). Treat any pinned model id in config as version-sensitive and confirm the current default before committing it.

[repo-setup] The 'frontier models reliably follow ~150-200 instructions' budget is a practitioner heuristic (HumanLayer), not an official Anthropic figure; the underlying context-degradation claim IS official, but the specific number should be treated as illustrative.

[repo-setup] Permission-enforcement is code, not model behavior, and bugs occur: a deny-rule bypass was patched in Claude Code v2.1.90 after a March 2026 source leak (reported by third parties). This argues for keeping the CLI current and not relying on permissions as the sole security layer — but the specific CVE details come from practitioner reporting rather than an official advisory and should be independently verified.

[repo-setup] Codex profile storage detail is ambiguous in the docs extraction (per-file $CODEX_HOME/<name>.config.toml vs [profiles.<name>] tables within config.toml); the reliable, confirmed facts are that profiles are selected with --profile <name> and a default is set via the profile key. Verify the exact on-disk form against the current Codex config reference before scripting it.

[repo-setup] MCP tool-search is on by default in Claude Code and changes how servers are surfaced to the model (ToolSearch/WaitForMcpServers); its defaults and interaction with large MCP tool sets are evolving and worth re-checking for teams wiring many servers.

[repo-setup] Sandboxing maturity differs by OS (e.g., Codex unified_exec noted as disabled on Windows; Claude Code WebDAV caveat on Windows). Cross-platform teams should validate sandbox behavior on each developer OS rather than assume parity.

[verification-self-checking] Whether the Codex apply_patch file-writer reliably triggers PreToolUse/PostToolUse hooks on all current versions. Official docs now say hooks fire for apply_patch, but an earlier gap (GitHub issue openai/codex #16732) let the agent edit test files via the patch tool despite Bash-only hook guards — so test-edit-blocking hooks may not be airtight depending on version.

[verification-self-checking] How universally the verify skill's 'don't run tests, don't typecheck at the done-gate' stance applies. It is a deliberate, somewhat contrarian Claude Code framing (tests validate infra, not surface behavior); the right split between in-loop tests and runtime-observation gating is still being worked out and is likely task-dependent.

[verification-self-checking] Best production combination for detecting reward hacking. EvilGenie found held-out tests added little over a strong LLM judge, while other work still recommends held-out/randomized tests plus fail-closed verifiers — the layered recipe (LLM-judge + test-edit detection + held-out tests + human review) is not yet standardized and each layer has known blind spots.

[verification-self-checking] There is no portable, cross-tool Definition-of-Done schema. Teams hand-roll it across AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, /goal conditions, and ad hoc Prompt.md/PLAN.md files; nothing standardizes the 'Done when' contract or makes it verifiable in the same way across Claude Code and Codex.

[verification-self-checking] Reward-hacking exploit rates rise with model capability (RL post-training increased exploit rates in several 2025-2026 benchmarks), so environment isolation and verifier hardening are an ongoing arms race rather than a solved problem — durable mitigations for autonomous production runs are still unsettled.

[subagent-orchestration] Codex enablement specifics: the official docs describe enabling multi-agents via the `/experimental` toggle and an `[agents]` config section, but the exact `[features] multi_agent = true` key and the default `job_max_runtime_seconds` value (practitioner posts say 1800s; one official extract listed the key without a number) should be confirmed against the current official Codex config.toml reference before relying on them.

[subagent-orchestration] Asynchronous / steerable orchestration: Anthropic's shipped system is synchronous (the lead blocks on each worker cohort) and they flagged async subagent creation + mid-run steering as future work in 2025 — the current production state of async orchestration (and whether Claude Code agent teams' live-messaging effectively delivers it) is unclear.

[subagent-orchestration] Transfer of effort-scaling numbers: Anthropic's fan-out heuristics (1 agent for fact-finding, 2-4 for comparisons, 10+ for complex research; 3-10 tool calls each) are calibrated to open-web research. How well these widths transfer to coding, data, or ops domains is not independently validated.

[subagent-orchestration] Production-readiness timeline: Claude Code agent teams remain experimental with material limitations (no in-process teammate resume, lagging task status, no nested teams). When/whether they graduate to stable, and whether the primitive converges with Codex's model, is unknown.

[subagent-orchestration] Reconciling the coding guidance: Anthropic and Cognition both argue against parallel subagents for implementation, yet both vendors ship coding-oriented subagent/team tooling. The empirical boundary — how disjoint file ownership must be, and at what task size parallel coding actually beats a single linear agent — lacks a published, quantified answer.

[workstream-logging] No cross-tool standard for the work-journal itself has emerged as of mid-2026 — teams roll their own (claude-progress.txt vs NOTES.md vs feature_list.json vs tasks/todo.md), so portability between Claude Code and Codex depends on self-imposed conventions rather than a shared spec.

[workstream-logging] Codex's official docs are thin on session storage internals and lifecycle commands; the ~/.codex/sessions/YYYY/MM/DD/rollout-*.jsonl path, `codex resume --last/--all`, and `/archive` -> ~/.codex/archived_sessions/ (v0.136.0, ~June 2026) are corroborated across practitioner sources but should be re-verified against the installed CLI version.

[workstream-logging] Claude Code does not persist a plan-mode plan as a first-class resumable artifact across sessions (only manual save via Ctrl+G); whether a durable, indexed plan/journal store becomes a native feature is unresolved.

[workstream-logging] The exact current inventory of OpenTelemetry metric and event names — and their minimum Claude Code versions — is version-sensitive and was partly read via doc summarization; confirm names against the live monitoring page before building alerts.

[workstream-logging] Per-event hook JSON input field names (e.g., tool_output, num_tool_calls, last_assistant_message) evolve between releases; scripts that parse them or the raw session JSONL can break on any version bump, so no stable machine-parseable logging contract exists yet beyond /export and the documented script interfaces.

[permissions-security] Prompt injection is not solved: Anthropic cites ~1% residual attack success and a measured ~17% false-negative rate for auto mode on real overeager actions, so no configuration makes an autonomous agent safe on untrusted input without OS-level containment.

[permissions-security] Network isolation is only as strong as TLS inspection: Claude's default sandbox proxy allows/denies by client-supplied hostname without terminating TLS, leaving domain-fronting bypasses; `network.tlsTerminate` is experimental (v2.1.199+) and stronger TLS-aware isolation is explicitly 'an active area of development'. Codex enforces network egress via seccomp syscall blocking rather than a domain-inspecting proxy.

[permissions-security] Version drift: Claude Code's auto-mode default block-list and many settings keys are feature-gated to exact 2.1.x versions (expanded through v2.1.205 as of July 2026), and Codex config keys differ across builds — always verify against the installed version rather than assuming.

[permissions-security] Native Windows has no built-in sandbox for either tool (Claude requires WSL2/bubblewrap; Codex Linux path needs WSL2), so Windows-host fleets need containers or WSL2 to get OS-level enforcement.

[permissions-security] Codex's exact per-domain network-egress allowlist mechanism (proxy/requirements.toml-style config) is less clearly documented in official sources than Claude's `sandbox.network.allowedDomains`, and appears version-dependent — confirm the current keys before relying on domain allowlisting in Codex.

[permissions-security] MCP servers are an unaudited trust boundary: neither vendor security-audits third-party MCP servers, so supply-chain risk in the MCP ecosystem is largely pushed onto the operator's allowlisting and vetting discipline.
